about: Landmarks in the map area, researched in November 2026 from Wikipedia (English first, Albanian where there is no English article), Wikidata and OpenStreetMap. Summaries are written for this map from those sources; follow the links for the full articles. Anchors: 'osm' = a clickable building (its OSM way), otherwise a label point.

landmarks.name: PTK headquarters
landmarks.summary: Head office of PTK, Kosovo's public post and telecommunications company. Its telecom arm, Telecom of Kosovo (trading as Vala), is the country's main fixed-line and internet provider; the postal service was split off as Posta e Kosovës in 2011–2012.

landmarks.name: Bill Clinton Boulevard
landmarks.summary: One of Prishtinë's main boulevards and the northern edge of Dardania; it used to be Lenin Street. After the 1998–99 war it was renamed to thank former US President Bill Clinton, and an 11-foot statue of him was unveiled on the boulevard in November 2009 with Clinton attending.

landmarks.name: Boulevard of the Nation's Martyrs
landmarks.summary: The main boulevard along Dardania's south-east side, formerly Marshal Tito Street. It carries most of the bus lines through this part of the city.

landmarks.name: Dardania
landmarks.summary: A central neighbourhood between Bill Clinton Boulevard and Dëshmorët e Kombit Boulevard. In 1946 it was a patch of private houses on the edge of a much smaller town; it was rebuilt as one of three planned modernist neighbourhoods (with Bregu i Diellit and Ulpiana), which is where the long apartment blocks come from.

landmarks.name: Ulpiana
landmarks.summary: A neighbourhood built in the same modernist plan as Dardania; its apartment blocks carry letter-and-number names like U1, A6 and C4. It is named after Ulpiana, an important Roman city about 12 km south-east of Prishtinë that is now an archaeological park.

landmarks.name: Hivzi Sylejmani Library
landmarks.summary: Prishtinë's municipal library, named after the Albanian writer Hivzi Sylejmani; the city library carried his name for decades. The building is listed as an architectural cultural-heritage monument.

landmarks.name: Bob Dole memorial
landmarks.summary: Memorial to US Senator Bob Dole (1923–2021), who lobbied for Kosovo Albanians before, during and after the 1998–99 war. The street beside it, Rruga Robert Doll, also carries his name.

landmarks.name: Henry Dunant monument
landmarks.summary: Monument to Henry Dunant (1828–1910), the Swiss humanitarian who co-founded the Red Cross and won the first Nobel Peace Prize in 1901.

landmarks.name: KOSTT
landmarks.local: Operatori i Sistemit, Transmisionit dhe Tregut
landmarks.summary: Head office of KOSTT, which runs Kosovo's high-voltage electricity transmission grid and its electricity market.

landmarks.name: KEDS
landmarks.local: Kompania Kosovare për Shpërndarje të Energjisë Elektrike
landmarks.summary: Kosovo's electricity distribution company. Founded in 2009, it became independent of the Kosovo Energy Corporation in May 2013 and is owned by the Turkish companies Çalık Holding and Limak.

landmarks.name: Tax Administration of Kosovo
landmarks.summary: Head office of the ATK, Kosovo's tax authority: an executive agency with full operational autonomy within the Ministry of Finance.

landmarks.name: Universum College
landmarks.summary: A university in Prishtinë, founded in 2005.

landmarks.name: IPKO Foundation
landmarks.summary: Foundation carrying the name of IPKO, Kosovo's second-largest mobile operator (owned by Telekom Slovenije).

landmarks.name: Catholic bishopric offices
landmarks.summary: Mapped in OpenStreetMap as offices of Kosovo's Catholic bishopric. Kosovo's Catholics belong to the Diocese of Prizren and Pristina, set up in 2000 and made a full diocese in 2018.

landmarks.name: British Council
landmarks.summary: Office of the British Council, the UK's organisation for international cultural and educational relations and English teaching.

landmarks.name: Embassy of Finland
landmarks.summary: Finland's embassy in Kosovo; OpenStreetMap places the Embassy of Sweden in the same building. There's no Wikipedia article about the embassy itself.
